task_1.title: Add ExceptionInfo.from_exception() classmethod as simplified alternative to from_exc_info()
task_1.description: Introduces a new classmethod ExceptionInfo.from_exception() that accepts a single exception object instead of the legacy (type, value, traceback) triplet required by from_exc_info(). This aligns with the Python 3.12 direction of soft-deprecating sys.exc_info()-style triplets, since all three components are derivable from the exception itself. The new method validates that the exception has a non-None __traceback__ attribute before proceeding. The existing from_exc_info() remains available but is repositioned as the lower-level alternative.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Creating an ExceptionInfo from a caught exception currently requires constructing a redundant (type(exc), exc, exc.__traceback__) triplet via from_exc_info(), even though all three components are derivable from the exception object alone. Ensure that ExceptionInfo provides a from_exception() classmethod that accepts a single exception object and produces the same ExceptionInfo result, simplifying the public API and aligning with the Python 3.12 soft-deprecation of sys.exc_info()-style triplets.

expectation.grounded: ExceptionInfo.from_exception(exception, exprinfo=None) must be a public classmethod on ExceptionInfo that returns an ExceptionInfo[E] instance. It must accept a single exception argument of generic type E and an optional exprinfo string parameter. It must raise an AssertionError if the exception's __traceback__ attribute is None. When __traceback__ is present, it must produce an ExceptionInfo equivalent to calling from_exc_info() with the derived triplet. The existing from_exc_info() classmethod must remain functional and continue to accept the (Type[E], E, TracebackType) triplet. Internal usage sites such as the raises() context manager and chained-exception formatting in FormattedExcinfo must use from_exception() instead of manually constructing triplets for from_exc_info().
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to create an ExceptionInfo directly from a caught exception object without manually assembling a type/value/traceback triplet. The new from_exception() method should behave identically to from_exc_info() in terms of the resulting ExceptionInfo, but with a simpler single-argument interface. The legacy from_exc_info() method should remain available for backward compatibility. Exceptions without a traceback should be rejected with a clear assertion failure.

constraints.grounded: from_exc_info() must not be removed or have its signature changed; it must continue to work as before. from_exception() must delegate to from_exc_info() internally, preserving the existing ExceptionInfo construction logic. The AssertionError stripping behavior controlled by the exprinfo parameter must work identically through both entry points. The from_exception() method must be generic over E (the exception type) consistent with ExceptionInfo's Generic[E] parameterization.
constraints.conceptual: The new method must not break any existing code that uses from_exc_info(). Both methods must produce functionally identical ExceptionInfo objects for the same exception. The validation of traceback presence must happen before any ExceptionInfo construction. No existing public API behavior should change.

behavior: Calling ExceptionInfo.from_exception(exc) where exc has a non-None __traceback__ returns an ExceptionInfo instance wrapping that exception, its type, and its traceback.
Calling ExceptionInfo.from_exception(exc) where exc.__traceback__ is None raises an AssertionError.

The optional exprinfo parameter on from_exception() is forwarded to the underlying construction logic and controls AssertionError message stripping, identical to the same parameter on from_exc_info().
ExceptionInfo.from_exc_info() continues to accept the (type, value, traceback) triplet and produces the same result as before.
pytest.raises() in callable form now internally uses from_exception() to construct its returned ExceptionInfo.
Chained exception formatting internally uses from_exception() when processing __cause__ and __context__ chains.
acceptance_criteria: When a raised exception with a valid traceback is passed to ExceptionInfo.from_exception(), it should return an ExceptionInfo whose value attribute is the original exception and whose tb attribute corresponds to the exception's __traceback__.
When an exception with __traceback__ set to None is passed to ExceptionInfo.from_exception(), it should raise an AssertionError.

When ExceptionInfo.from_exception(exc, exprinfo='custom') is called, the resulting ExceptionInfo should handle the exprinfo parameter identically to from_exc_info((type(exc), exc, exc.__traceback__), exprinfo='custom').
When ExceptionInfo.from_exc_info() is called with a valid triplet, it should continue to return a correct ExceptionInfo as before the change.
When pytest.raises(SomeException)(some_callable) catches an exception, it should return an ExceptionInfo equivalent to the previous behavior but constructed via from_exception().
When formatting chained exceptions (via __cause__ or __context__), the formatter should use from_exception() and produce output identical to the previous triplet-based approach.

task_2.title: Introduce TestShortLogReport NamedTuple and fix pytest_report_teststatus return type
task_2.description: The return type annotation of the pytest_report_teststatus hook was incorrect and inconsistent with its documented example. The third element (word) was typed as Union[str, Mapping[str, bool]], but the actual usage and examples showed it could also be a Tuple[str, Mapping[str, bool]]. This update introduces a new TestShortLogReport NamedTuple as the structured return type for the hook, corrects the word field type to Union[str, Tuple[str, Mapping[str, bool]]], and exports the new type as part of the public pytest API. The hook now accepts both the new NamedTuple and the corrected plain tuple form.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the pytest_report_teststatus hook return type correctly reflects all valid return shapes, including the case where the verbose word element is a tuple of a string and a markup mapping. Ensure that a structured NamedTuple (TestShortLogReport) is available as the canonical return type so that hook consumers and implementers can use named field access (category, letter, word) instead of positional indexing.

expectation.grounded: A new public NamedTuple class TestShortLogReport with fields category (str), letter (str), and word (Union[str, Tuple[str, Mapping[str, bool]]]) is exported from the pytest top-level namespace. The pytest_report_teststatus hook's return type annotation accepts either TestShortLogReport or a plain tuple with the corrected word type. Internally, TerminalReporter.pytest_runtest_logreport wraps the hook result in TestShortLogReport for structured field access. Existing hook implementations returning plain tuples continue to function without modification.
expectation.conceptual: The test status reporting hook gains a structured, self-documenting return type with named fields for category, letter, and word. The word field type is corrected to also accept a tuple containing a display string and a markup-flag mapping. The new NamedTuple is publicly accessible so plugin authors can use it. Backward compatibility with plain tuple returns is preserved.

constraints.grounded: Existing pytest_report_teststatus hook implementations that return a plain 3-tuple must continue to work without any changes. The TestShortLogReport NamedTuple must remain tuple-compatible (i.e., it is a NamedTuple, so unpacking and indexing still work). The corrected word type must accept both str and Tuple[str, Mapping[str, bool]] forms. TestShortLogReport must be importable from the top-level pytest package and present in __all__.
constraints.conceptual: Backward compatibility with existing hook implementations must be preserved. The new type must be accessible as a first-class public API. Both simple string words and styled word tuples must be supported. No existing plugin or user code should break due to this change.

behavior: TestShortLogReport is a NamedTuple with three fields: category (str), letter (str), and word (Union[str, Tuple[str, Mapping[str, bool]]])
TestShortLogReport is exported from the top-level pytest namespace and listed in __all__
The pytest_report_teststatus hook return type annotation now accepts TestShortLogReport or a corrected plain tuple type
The word field type is corrected from Union[str, Mapping[str, bool]] to Union[str, Tuple[str, Mapping[str, bool]]], matching the documented example of ("RERUN", {"yellow": True})
TerminalReporter.pytest_runtest_logreport wraps the hook result into a TestShortLogReport instance, enabling named field access (res.category, res.letter, res.word)
Existing hook implementations returning plain 3-tuples are accepted via unpacking into the NamedTuple constructor
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin implements pytest_report_teststatus and returns a plain 3-tuple like ("passed", ".", "PASSED"), the test session runs without errors
When a plugin returns a 3-tuple with a styled word like ("rerun", "R", ("RERUN", {"yellow": True})), the test session runs without errors and the styled word is rendered correctly
When a plugin returns a TestShortLogReport instance, the test session runs without errors
When importing TestShortLogReport from pytest (i.e., pytest.TestShortLogReport), it resolves to the NamedTuple class with fields category, letter, and word
When unpacking a TestShortLogReport instance (category, letter, word = report), it yields the same values as positional tuple access
When inspecting the pytest_report_teststatus hook spec return type, the word element type includes Union[str, Tuple[str, Mapping[str, bool]]] rather than the previous Union[str, Mapping[str, bool]]

task_4.title: Wrap verbose skip/xfail reasons to preserve progress percentage alignment
task_4.description: In verbose mode (-vv and above), skip and xfail reason strings could exceed the terminal width, pushing the right-aligned progress percentage (e.g., '[ 49%]') onto the next line and breaking visual alignment with surrounding results. This change introduces text wrapping for those reason strings, reserving a fixed margin so the progress indicator stays consistently right-aligned on every output line, even when the reason text spans multiple lines.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest is run in verbose mode (-vv or higher), skip and xfail reason strings that exceed the terminal width are wrapped across multiple lines while keeping the right-aligned progress percentage column consistently aligned with single-line results.

expectation.grounded: TerminalReporter exposes a new public helper method wrap_write() that accepts content, flush, margin, line_sep, and markup keyword arguments. When skip or xfail reasons are displayed in verbose mode, they are emitted through wrap_write() instead of the plain write() path. wrap_write() uses textwrap.wrap with a width equal to the screen width minus the margin (default 8 characters), accounts for the width already consumed on the current line, preserves non-space whitespace (replace_whitespace=False), and drops leading/trailing whitespace from wrapped segments (drop_whitespace=True). The resulting wrapped text, when combined with the progress suffix, produces lines that do not exceed the terminal width.
expectation.conceptual: When a skip or xfail reason is long enough to exceed the terminal width in verbose output, pytest should automatically wrap the reason text across multiple lines. Each line should leave enough trailing space so that the progress percentage indicator remains right-aligned at the same column as all other test result lines. The wrapping should respect the current cursor position on the line so the first wrapped segment begins seamlessly after the test status word.

constraints.grounded: The existing TerminalReporter.write() method must remain unchanged and continue to function for all non-wrapped output. wrap_write() must not alter markup or flush semantics—these are forwarded to the underlying TerminalWriter.write(). The margin default of 8 characters must accommodate the widest standard progress suffix (e.g., ' [100%]' is 7 characters plus a leading space). Short reason strings that fit within a single line must not be padded or altered beyond normal write behavior. The wrap_write() method must be a public method on TerminalReporter so plugins and extensions can also use it.
constraints.conceptual: Existing terminal output for non-verbose modes and for reasons that fit on a single line must not change. The wrapping must not corrupt markup styling or suppress flush behavior. The reserved margin must be wide enough to hold the progress percentage string in all cases. The feature must not break plugin compatibility with the terminal reporter interface.

behavior: In verbose mode (-vv+), skip and xfail reason strings longer than (terminal_width - margin) are wrapped onto multiple lines instead of being emitted as a single long line.
Each wrapped line except the last is padded so that any appended progress suffix would appear at the rightmost column, preserving alignment with adjacent single-line results.
The first wrapped segment accounts for the text already printed on the current line (e.g., the test path and status), so wrapping breaks occur at the correct position.

Non-space whitespace characters (e.g., newlines already in the reason) are preserved during wrapping (replace_whitespace=False), while leading/trailing spaces on wrapped segments are dropped (drop_whitespace=True).
A new public method TerminalReporter.wrap_write() is available, accepting content, flush, margin (default 8), line_sep (default newline), and arbitrary boolean markup keyword arguments.
When reason strings are short enough to fit on a single line with the progress suffix, output is visually identical to prior behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest with -vv and a test is skipped with a reason string longer than the terminal width, the output wraps the reason across multiple lines and the progress percentage appears right-aligned on the last line at the same column as other results.
When running pytest with -vv and a test is marked xfail with a long reason, the same wrapping and alignment behavior applies.
When a skip or xfail reason fits within a single line, the output is unchanged compared to previous behavior.
TerminalReporter.wrap_write() is callable with content, margin, line_sep, flush, and markup keyword arguments and produces correctly wrapped output that respects the current cursor position.
The default margin of 8 characters in wrap_write() is sufficient to accommodate the progress suffix (e.g., ' [100%]') without overlap.
Existing non-verbose mode output and verbose output without skip/xfail reasons are unaffected by the change.
Markup styling (e.g., color) passed through wrap_write() is correctly forwarded to the underlying terminal writer.

task_5.title: Support %f (microseconds) in log date format options
task_5.description: Previously, using the %f strftime directive in pytest log date format options (such as --log-date-format, --log-cli-date-format, --log-file-date-format) resulted in the literal string '%f' appearing in log output instead of the microsecond value. This is because Python's time.strftime does not support %f; only datetime.datetime.strftime does. A new DatetimeFormatter class was introduced that detects %f in the date format string and switches to datetime-based formatting, enabling sub-second timestamp precision across all pytest log outputs. This allows users to correlate pytest log messages with other system logs that use sub-second timestamps.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the %f strftime directive is properly handled in all pytest log date format options (--log-date-format, --log-cli-date-format, --log-file-date-format) so that microsecond values are rendered in log timestamps instead of the literal string '%f'. Previously, specifying %f in any log date format option produced the literal text '%f' in log output, preventing users from achieving sub-second timestamp granularity needed to correlate pytest logs with external system logs.

expectation.grounded: When %f is included in any log date format setting, the DatetimeFormatter.formatTime method should construct a datetime.datetime object from the LogRecord's created timestamp and msecs field, then use datetime.strftime to produce the formatted time string with microsecond resolution. When %f is not present in the date format, formatting should fall back to the standard logging.Formatter.formatTime behavior. This applies to all log output paths: terminal (colored and non-colored) and file logging. ColoredLevelFormatter must inherit from DatetimeFormatter to gain this capability.
expectation.conceptual: When a user specifies %f in any pytest log date format option, log timestamps should include the actual microsecond component of the log event time. When %f is not used, log formatting behavior should remain identical to previous versions. The feature must work consistently across CLI log output, terminal log capture, and file-based log output.

constraints.grounded: When the date format string does not contain %f, DatetimeFormatter must delegate to the parent logging.Formatter.formatTime, preserving existing behavior exactly. The microsecond value must be derived from the LogRecord's msecs attribute (converted to microseconds) to maintain consistency with the record's created timestamp. Timezone information must be preserved from the converter's struct_time output. All formatter instantiation points (log file formatter, non-colored terminal formatter, and ColoredLevelFormatter) must use DatetimeFormatter or a subclass thereof.
constraints.conceptual: Existing log date formatting behavior must not change for users who do not use %f. Timezone correctness must be maintained in all formatted timestamps. The feature must apply uniformly to all log output destinations that accept date format configuration.

behavior: When %f is present in the datefmt string, formatTime constructs a timezone-aware datetime object from the log record and formats it using datetime.strftime, producing actual microsecond digits in the output.
When %f is not present in the datefmt string, formatTime delegates to the standard logging.Formatter.formatTime, preserving backward-compatible behavior.
The colored level formatter for terminal output inherits microsecond formatting capability through the new DatetimeFormatter base class.
The log file formatter uses DatetimeFormatter instead of logging.Formatter, enabling %f support in --log-file-date-format.
The non-colored terminal formatter uses DatetimeFormatter instead of logging.Formatter, enabling %f support in --log-date-format and --log-cli-date-format.
Microsecond values are derived by converting the LogRecord's msecs field (milliseconds) to microseconds, ensuring alignment with the record's created timestamp.
acceptance_criteria: When --log-cli-date-format includes %f (e.g., '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f'), CLI log output should display timestamps with actual microsecond digits instead of the literal string '%f'.
When --log-file-date-format includes %f, log file output should display timestamps with actual microsecond digits.
When --log-date-format includes %f, all log outputs using the general date format should display timestamps with actual microsecond digits.
When no %f directive is present in any date format option, log timestamp formatting should remain unchanged from prior behavior.
Microsecond values in timestamps should accurately reflect the sub-second component of the actual log event time.
Timezone information in formatted timestamps should be correct and consistent with the logging system's configured time converter.
Colored terminal log output should support %f in the same way as non-colored output.

task_3.title: Gracefully handle fully-hidden exception tracebacks
task_3.description: When all traceback entries in an exception are hidden (via __tracebackhide__, internal-frame filtering, or similar mechanisms), pytest previously displayed the last frame of the traceback even though it was marked hidden. This change makes pytest instead show only the exception string and a guidance message directing the user to use --full-trace. Internally, the traceback infrastructure was refactored to an immutable/functional style: TracebackEntry is now immutable, _prunetraceback was replaced by _traceback_filter returning a new Traceback instead of mutating ExceptionInfo, the Traceback and TracebackEntry classes no longer hold weak references to ExceptionInfo, and the tbfilter parameter on getrepr now accepts a callable for custom filtering.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when all traceback entries for an exception are hidden (e.g., via __tracebackhide__ or internal-frame filtering), pytest no longer displays a hidden frame. Instead, only the exception details and a message instructing the user to pass --full-trace should be shown. Ensure that the traceback filtering and representation pipeline supports fully-empty tracebacks gracefully, that the crash location (reprcrash) may be absent when no visible frame exists, and that custom traceback filter callables can be supplied via the tbfilter parameter.

expectation.grounded: When all TracebackEntry items in a Traceback are hidden after applying the filter (via Traceback.filter with an ExceptionInfo or callable), FormattedExcinfo.repr_traceback should produce a ReprTraceback containing a single ReprEntry with only the exception message lines (no source/file location) and an extraline reading 'All traceback entries are hidden. Pass `--full-trace` to see hidden and internal frames.' ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash should return None when every entry is hidden. ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash is now Optional[ReprFileLocation]. Traceback.filter no longer has a default argument; callers must pass an ExceptionInfo or a callable. TracebackEntry.ishidden now requires an explicit excinfo argument. The getrepr method's tbfilter parameter accepts Union[bool, Callable[[ExceptionInfo], Traceback]]. The _traceback_filter method on Node, Function, Collector, and TestCaseFunction returns a Traceback rather than mutating excinfo.traceback in place.
expectation.conceptual: When every traceback frame is suppressed, the user should see only the exception type and message, followed by a hint about how to reveal the full trace. No hidden frame content should leak into the output. The traceback filtering mechanism should support both the built-in hiding logic and user-supplied custom filter functions. Crash location metadata should be absent rather than point to a hidden frame when all frames are hidden.

constraints.grounded: When --full-trace is passed, all traceback entries must still be shown regardless of __tracebackhide__ markers; the empty-traceback path must not be triggered. TracebackEntry must remain immutable after construction: _repr_style is set at creation or via with_repr_style which returns a new instance. Traceback.getcrashentry is removed; crash-entry resolution is handled by ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash. The Traceback class must not store a reference (weak or otherwise) to ExceptionInfo. ReprEntry.toterminal must not assert on reprfileloc being non-None for short style. For skip exceptions, _getreprcrash must return a non-None ReprFileLocation. When tbfilter is a callable, repr_traceback must invoke it with the ExceptionInfo to obtain the filtered Traceback. When tbfilter is True, repr_traceback must call traceback.filter(excinfo). When tbfilter is False, no filtering is applied. Native traceback style (--tb=native) must handle an empty traceback without error by passing None as the traceback argument to format_exception.
constraints.conceptual: Full-trace mode must bypass all hiding and always display every frame. The traceback data model must not retain circular or weak references between traceback objects and exception info. Crash location reporting must never expose hidden frames. Skip-exception tracebacks must always have a resolvable crash location. Custom filter callables must be invoked transparently without altering the default filtering behavior when not supplied. Native traceback formatting must degrade gracefully when the traceback is empty.

behavior: When all traceback entries are hidden, the displayed output contains only the exception string (e.g., 'E   ZeroDivisionError: division by zero') followed by the message 'All traceback entries are hidden. Pass `--full-trace` to see hidden and internal frames.'
The previously shown last-hidden-frame is no longer displayed when all entries are filtered out.
ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash returns None instead of a ReprFileLocation when every traceback entry is hidden.
ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash is Optional and may be None.
Traceback.filter requires an explicit ExceptionInfo or callable argument; the no-argument default has been removed.
TracebackEntry.ishidden now takes an explicit ExceptionInfo parameter rather than reading from an internal weak reference.
TracebackEntry is immutable: _rawentry and _repr_style are Final; with_repr_style returns a new TracebackEntry.
The mutable set_repr_style method on TracebackEntry is removed, replaced by the immutable with_repr_style factory.
Traceback.getcrashentry is removed; its logic is inlined into ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash with None-return support.
The Traceback constructor and TracebackEntry constructor no longer accept or store an excinfo weak reference.
Node._prunetraceback is renamed to Node._traceback_filter and returns a Traceback instead of mutating excinfo.traceback.
getrepr's tbfilter parameter accepts a callable for custom traceback filtering in addition to bool.
FormattedExcinfo.repr_traceback_entry accepts None as the entry parameter for rendering empty-traceback placeholders.
ReprEntry.toterminal no longer asserts reprfileloc is non-None for short style; it conditionally renders it.
Native traceback formatting (--tb=native) passes None as the traceback to format_exception when the traceback is empty.
acceptance_criteria: When a test raises an exception and all traceback entries are hidden via __tracebackhide__, the output should contain only the exception string and the message 'All traceback entries are hidden. Pass `--full-trace` to see hidden and internal frames.' with no source code lines or file locations from hidden frames.
When a test raises an exception and all traceback entries are hidden, running with --full-trace should display the complete traceback including all previously hidden frames.
When some but not all traceback entries are hidden, the visible entries should be displayed normally with no behavioral change from the standard filtering.
When a custom callable is passed as tbfilter to getrepr, it should receive the ExceptionInfo and its returned Traceback should be used for rendering.
When tbfilter is True (default), traceback filtering should use the excinfo-based ishidden logic on each entry.
When tbfilter is False, no entries should be filtered and all frames should appear.
When using --tb=native and all traceback entries are hidden, the output should not raise an error and should degrade gracefully.
When a test is skipped, the crash location (reprcrash) should always be non-None regardless of hidden entries.
TracebackEntry instances should be immutable: calling with_repr_style should return a new instance rather than modifying the original.
Traceback.filter called without arguments should raise a TypeError (no default parameter).
The repr output for fully-hidden tracebacks should not contain any file paths, line numbers, or source code from hidden frames.

task_6.title: Include underlying OS error in cache provider warning messages
task_6.description: Previously, when pytest's cache provider failed to create a cache directory or write a cache file, the emitted warnings only stated that the operation failed, without indicating the reason. This made it difficult for users to diagnose caching issues (e.g., permission errors, disk full, read-only filesystems). The cache provider now appends the underlying OSError to both the path-creation and file-write warning messages, giving users actionable diagnostic information.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when the Cache provider encounters an OSError during cache path creation or cache file writing, the resulting warning message includes the underlying exception's description so that users can diagnose the root cause of cache failures without additional investigation.

expectation.grounded: When Cache.set() fails to create the cache directory (OSError on mkdir), the warning emitted via Cache.warn() must include the string representation of the caught OSError after the path information. When Cache.set() fails to open the cache file for writing (OSError on file open), the warning emitted via Cache.warn() must likewise include the string representation of the caught OSError. Both warning messages must still contain the target path. The warning call must use direct string formatting rather than keyword-based path interpolation.
expectation.conceptual: When a cache write operation fails due to an OS-level error, the warning message presented to the user should clearly state both which path was affected and what the underlying operating system error was, enabling the user to understand and resolve the issue without further debugging.

constraints.grounded: The Cache provider must continue to catch OSError for both directory creation and file write operations and must not propagate the exception to the caller. The method must still return early (skip writing) when directory creation fails, and must still ensure supporting files are created when the cache directory is newly created. The warning must be issued through the existing Cache.warn() mechanism. No new exception types or warning categories should be introduced.
constraints.conceptual: Cache write failures must remain non-fatal; the test session must not be interrupted by a caching error. The improvement must only affect the content of existing warning messages and must not alter control flow, error handling boundaries, or the public API surface of the cache provider.

behavior: When an OSError occurs during cache directory creation, the warning message now contains the OS error description appended after the cache path.
When an OSError occurs during cache file opening for write, the warning message now contains the OS error description appended after the cache path.
The underlying OSError is captured in both except clauses to enable inclusion in the message.
Warning messages use direct f-string formatting with the exception embedded, replacing the previous keyword-based path interpolation style.
acceptance_criteria: When Cache.set() is called and mkdir raises an OSError (e.g., PermissionError), the emitted warning message should contain the cache path AND the OS error reason string.
When Cache.set() is called and opening the cache file for writing raises an OSError (e.g., PermissionError), the emitted warning message should contain the cache path AND the OS error reason string.
When cache directory creation fails with an OSError, Cache.set() should return without writing data and without raising an exception.
When cache file writing fails with an OSError, Cache.set() should not raise an exception to the caller.
Given a successful cache write operation, no warnings should be emitted and behavior should be unchanged from the prior version.
The warning messages must be issued through the standard Cache.warn() interface and remain visible in pytest's standard warning output.

task_9.title: Move norecursedirs check into pytest_ignore_collect hook
task_9.description: The norecursedirs directory exclusion check was previously performed inline within the Session and Package collectors' _recurse methods. It has been relocated into the centralized pytest_ignore_collect hook implementation in main. This reduces duplication, improves decoupling, and—critically—allows plugins to participate in or override the norecursedirs behavior through the standard hook chain. However, plugins that incorrectly return False (instead of None) from pytest_ignore_collect for paths they do not wish to ignore may now inadvertently short-circuit the hook chain, preventing the norecursedirs check from ever running.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the norecursedirs configuration is enforced via the pytest_ignore_collect hook rather than being hard-coded inside individual collector classes. This allows plugins and conftest files to influence or override norecursedirs behavior through the standard hook mechanism. Ensure that directories matching norecursedirs patterns are still correctly excluded from collection. Ensure that the check only applies to directory paths, not files. Ensure that plugins returning None (rather than False) from pytest_ignore_collect do not interfere with the norecursedirs enforcement.

expectation.grounded: The pytest_ignore_collect hook should evaluate the norecursedirs configuration patterns against directory-typed collection_path arguments and return True when a match is found, causing the directory to be ignored. The Session._recurse and Package._recurse methods should no longer independently check norecursedirs patterns. The hook should return None (not False) when norecursedirs patterns do not match, allowing the hook chain to continue for other implementations. The fnmatch_ex function is used for pattern matching against norecursedirs entries retrieved via config.getini('norecursedirs').
expectation.conceptual: The norecursedirs exclusion logic should be centralized within the standard collection-ignoring hook rather than duplicated across individual collector types. Plugins implementing the same hook can now run before or after this check and influence the outcome. The exclusion check should only apply to directories. The hook should yield control to subsequent hook implementations when no norecursedirs pattern matches.

constraints.grounded: Directories matching norecursedirs patterns must still be excluded from test collection—the observable behavior for users who do not have custom pytest_ignore_collect hooks must remain unchanged. The check must only fire for directory paths (collection_path.is_dir()). The hook must return None (not False) for non-matching paths to avoid terminating the hook call chain. Plugins whose pytest_ignore_collect returns False for paths they do not want to ignore will break the norecursedirs enforcement—this is a known behavioral contract change.
constraints.conceptual: Existing users relying on norecursedirs without custom plugins must see no change in directory exclusion behavior. The refactoring must not alter the semantics of file-level collection. Plugin authors must use None (not False) as the non-ignore return value from their pytest_ignore_collect implementations to preserve correct hook chain behavior.

behavior: The norecursedirs check is removed from Session._recurse and Package._recurse and consolidated into the pytest_ignore_collect hook.
When pytest_ignore_collect is invoked with a directory path matching any norecursedirs pattern, it returns True, causing that directory to be skipped during collection.

When pytest_ignore_collect is invoked with a directory path that does not match any norecursedirs pattern, or with a file path, the norecursedirs block is not triggered and the hook returns None, allowing other hook implementations to proceed.

Plugins with pytest_ignore_collect implementations that return False (instead of None) for paths they do not wish to ignore will short-circuit the hook chain and prevent the norecursedirs check from executing, potentially causing previously excluded directories to be collected.
acceptance_criteria: When norecursedirs is configured with a pattern and a directory matching that pattern exists, running pytest should exclude that directory from collection, same as before the change.
When a plugin implements pytest_ignore_collect and returns None for unrecognized paths, the norecursedirs exclusion should still be enforced for matching directories.
When a plugin implements pytest_ignore_collect and incorrectly returns False for unrecognized paths, the norecursedirs exclusion may not be enforced—this is expected new behavior.
When norecursedirs patterns are configured, file paths should not be evaluated against them within the pytest_ignore_collect hook; only directory paths should be checked.
When no norecursedirs patterns match the collection directory, the pytest_ignore_collect hook should return None, not False, preserving the hook chain for subsequent implementations.

task_8.title: Default confcutdir falls back to rootdir when no config file is present
task_8.description: When --confcutdir is not explicitly specified and no configuration file (e.g., pyproject.toml, pytest.ini) is present, pytest now sets the conftest cutoff directory to the rootdir instead of leaving it unset. Previously, the absence of both --confcutdir and a config file meant there was no cutoff, causing pytest to probe for conftest.py files all the way up to the filesystem root directory. This change limits conftest discovery to the rootdir and below, which is a safer and more predictable default but may alter behavior for projects that relied on conftest.py files located above the rootdir.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when --confcutdir is not explicitly provided and no configuration file is detected, pytest defaults the conftest cutoff directory to the rootdir rather than leaving it unbounded. Previously, conftest.py files were probed up to the filesystem root, which could cause unexpected side effects from stray conftest files in ancestor directories. Users who rely on conftest files above the rootdir should either add an empty config file at the desired cutoff point or explicitly set --confcutdir.

expectation.grounded: When Config initializes and known_args_namespace.confcutdir is None: if inipath is set, confcutdir should be set to inipath.parent (existing behavior); if inipath is not set, confcutdir should fall back to rootpath. In all cases, known_args_namespace.confcutdir must be assigned a non-None value before pytest_load_initial_conftests is invoked. The --confcutdir CLI option, when explicitly provided, continues to take precedence over both fallbacks.
expectation.conceptual: When no explicit conftest cutoff directory is configured and no configuration file is present, the conftest discovery boundary should default to the project root directory. Conftest files located in directories above the project root should no longer be loaded automatically. Explicit user-provided --confcutdir values should always override the default behavior.

constraints.grounded: When --confcutdir is explicitly provided by the user, neither the inipath-based nor the rootpath-based fallback should override it. When a config file is present (inipath is not None), confcutdir must still resolve to inipath.parent, preserving pre-existing behavior. The confcutdir value must be set before the pytest_load_initial_conftests hook fires, so that conftest probing respects the cutoff from the start.
constraints.conceptual: Explicit user configuration must always take priority over any automatic defaults. Projects with a configuration file must see no change in conftest discovery behavior. The conftest cutoff must be established before any conftest loading begins to prevent partial or inconsistent conftest discovery.

behavior: When --confcutdir is not specified and no config file (inipath) exists, confcutdir is now set to rootpath instead of remaining None.
When confcutdir was previously None, conftest.py files were discovered up to the filesystem root; now discovery stops at the rootdir.
When --confcutdir is not specified but a config file exists, confcutdir continues to be set to the config file's parent directory (no change).
When --confcutdir is explicitly specified, the user-provided value is used regardless of config file or rootdir presence (no change).
Conftest.py files located in directories above the rootdir are no longer loaded in the no-config-file scenario.
acceptance_criteria: When --confcutdir is not set and no config file is present, confcutdir should equal the rootdir.
When --confcutdir is not set and a config file is present, confcutdir should equal the config file's parent directory.
When --confcutdir is explicitly set, the explicit value should be used regardless of config file presence.
Given a conftest.py file located in a directory above the rootdir, when pytest runs without --confcutdir and without a config file, then that conftest.py should not be loaded.
Given a conftest.py file located within or at the rootdir, when pytest runs without --confcutdir and without a config file, then that conftest.py should still be loaded normally.
Given a conftest.py file located above the rootdir, when pytest runs with --confcutdir explicitly pointing above the rootdir, then that conftest.py should still be loaded.

task_7.title: Warn when testpaths config does not match any files or directories
task_7.description: When the pytest 'testpaths' configuration option is set but its glob patterns do not match any existing files or directories, pytest previously fell back silently to searching recursively from the current directory. This made misconfigured testpaths hard to diagnose. A PytestConfigWarning is now emitted in this scenario, alerting users that their testpaths did not resolve to anything and that pytest is falling back to current-directory search. The fallback behavior itself is preserved for backward compatibility.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when the 'testpaths' configuration value is set but its glob patterns match no files or directories, pytest emits a warning to the user before falling back to recursive search from the current directory. Previously, this fallback was entirely silent, making it difficult for users to detect misconfigured testpaths (e.g., referencing a directory that does not exist).

expectation.grounded: When Config parses arguments and 'testpaths' is configured (non-empty), but the glob expansion of all testpaths entries yields zero results, Config._decide_args should trigger a PytestConfigWarning via Config.issue_config_time_warning. The warning should indicate that no files were found in testpaths and that pytest is searching from the current directory instead. The args-decision logic (previously inlined in Config.parse) must be consolidated into Config._decide_args and reused by both Config.parse (with warn=True) and Config.pytest_load_initial_conftests (with warn=False). The ArgsSource should be set to INCOVATION_DIR when falling back.
expectation.conceptual: When a user configures testpaths but the specified paths do not exist or match nothing, pytest should emit a visible configuration warning before falling back to its default directory-search behavior. The warning should clearly communicate that the configured testpaths were ineffective and describe what pytest is doing instead. Early conftest discovery should use the same path-resolution logic as the main argument parsing phase but without emitting warnings at that early stage.

constraints.grounded: The warning must only be issued during the main parse phase (warn=True), not during the early pytest_load_initial_conftests phase (warn=False). The warning must be of type PytestConfigWarning. When explicit args are provided on the command line (ArgsSource.ARGS), no testpaths warning should be emitted. When pyargs is active, testpaths should be used as-is without glob expansion. When the invocation directory differs from rootpath, testpaths should not be consulted at all. The silent fallback to invocation_dir must still occur; the warning is additive, not replacing the fallback behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The warning must not appear when users explicitly provide test paths on the command line. The fallback to searching from the current directory must remain intact for backward compatibility. The warning must only appear once during argument resolution, not during preliminary conftest discovery. The feature must not change collection behavior, only add observability for misconfigured testpaths.

behavior: When testpaths is configured and all glob patterns resolve to zero paths, a PytestConfigWarning is emitted during the parse phase
The warning message indicates that no files were found in testpaths and that pytest is searching recursively from the current directory instead
After emitting the warning, pytest falls back to using the invocation directory as the search root (ArgsSource set to INCOVATION_DIR), preserving existing fallback behavior
When explicit file_or_dir arguments are provided on the command line, testpaths is not consulted and no warning is emitted
When invocation_dir differs from rootpath, testpaths is not consulted regardless of configuration
When pyargs is active, testpaths values are used directly without glob expansion, so no glob-based warning is triggered
The args-decision logic is consolidated into Config._decide_args, which is called both during early conftest loading (warn=False) and during full argument parsing (warn=True)
The pytest_load_initial_conftests hook now resolves args through _decide_args before passing them to _set_initial_conftests, ensuring consistent path resolution across both phases
acceptance_criteria: When testpaths is set to a non-existent directory name in the config and no command-line args are provided, running pytest should emit a PytestConfigWarning mentioning that no files were found in testpaths
When testpaths is set to a non-existent directory name, pytest should still proceed to collect tests from the current directory (fallback behavior preserved)
When testpaths is set to an existing directory that matches the glob, no warning should be emitted and pytest should collect from that directory as before
When explicit test paths are passed on the command line, no testpaths-related warning should be emitted regardless of testpaths configuration
When pytest is invoked from a subdirectory different from rootpath, no testpaths-related warning should be emitted even if testpaths is configured
When pyargs is active, testpaths values should be used without glob expansion and no glob-miss warning should be emitted
The warning should not appear during conftest discovery (early phase), only during the main argument parsing phase
The warning type must be PytestConfigWarning so users can filter or suppress it using standard pytest warning controls

task_10.title: caplog.set_level and caplog.at_level override logging.disable
task_10.description: When logging.disable(LEVEL) was called globally (e.g., in Django test settings), caplog.set_level() and caplog.at_level() would fail to capture logs at the requested level because logging.disable is a separate mechanism from individual logger levels. This change makes both methods temporarily re-enable logging at the requested level so that caplog can capture messages even when a global disable is in effect, and restores the original disabled level when the test or context manager finishes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that caplog.set_level() and caplog.at_level() can capture log records at the requested level even when logging has been globally suppressed via logging.disable(LEVEL). Previously, calling logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) before a test prevented caplog from capturing any logs regardless of the level passed to set_level or at_level, forcing users to manually call logging.disable as a workaround.

expectation.grounded: When caplog.set_level(level, logger) or caplog.at_level(level, logger) is called and the requested level is disabled via the global logging.disable mechanism (i.e., logger.isEnabledFor(level) returns False), the LogCaptureFixture must invoke logging.disable with a value of max(level - 10, logging.NOTSET) to re-enable logging at the requested level and above. If a non-standard level string is provided that cannot be resolved to an integer, logging.disable(logging.NOTSET) should be called to fully re-enable logging. The original disabled logging level must be stored in _initial_disabled_logging_level. Upon finalization of set_level (via _finalize) or upon exiting the at_level context manager, the original disabled logging level must be restored via logging.disable. The _force_enable_logging method must read the current disable level from logger_obj.manager.disable, accept both int and str level arguments, and return the original disable level.
expectation.conceptual: When a test requests log capture at a specific level using caplog.set_level() or caplog.at_level(), the fixture should automatically override any global logging suppression so that logs at the requested level and above are captured. When the test completes or the context manager exits, the original global suppression state should be restored so that other tests are unaffected.

constraints.grounded: The original disabled logging level must always be restored after the test or context block completes, ensuring no side effects leak across tests. If logging was not globally disabled (i.e., the requested level is already enabled for the logger), _force_enable_logging must not alter the global disable level. The _initial_disabled_logging_level must only be recorded on the first call to set_level to preserve the true original state across multiple calls. The at_level context manager must restore the disabled level in its finally block independently of _finalize. String-based levels that resolve to valid integers must be handled identically to integer levels.
constraints.conceptual: Global logging suppression state must be fully restored after each test to prevent cross-test interference. The override should be minimal — only enabling the requested level and above, not all logging. If logging was not globally suppressed, the behavior of set_level and at_level must remain unchanged from prior versions.

behavior: caplog.set_level(level) temporarily calls logging.disable(max(level - 10, NOTSET)) when the requested level is globally disabled, enabling capture at that level and above

caplog.at_level(level) as a context manager temporarily calls logging.disable(max(level - 10, NOTSET)) when the requested level is globally disabled, and restores the original disable level on context exit
If a non-standard string level is passed that cannot be resolved to an integer, logging is fully re-enabled via logging.disable(NOTSET)
If the requested level is already enabled for the logger (not globally disabled), no change is made to the global disable level
The LogCaptureFixture._finalize method restores the original disabled logging level saved during set_level, ensuring cleanup at test teardown
The initial disabled logging level is captured only once (on the first set_level call) to preserve the true original state
acceptance_criteria: Given logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) has been called globally, when caplog.set_level(logging.WARNING) is invoked, then caplog should capture log records at WARNING level and above

Given logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) has been called globally, when using 'with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING)' as a context manager, then caplog should capture log records at WARNING level and above within the block

Given logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) has been called and caplog.set_level(logging.WARNING) was used in a test, when the test finalizes, then the global disable level should be restored to logging.CRITICAL

Given logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) has been called and 'with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING)' is used, when the context manager exits, then the global disable level should be restored to logging.CRITICAL
Given logging has not been globally disabled, when caplog.set_level(logging.WARNING) is called, then the behavior should be identical to previous versions with no changes to the global disable level

Given logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) has been called, when caplog.set_level is called multiple times with different levels, then the original disabled level from before the first call should be restored during finalization
Given a non-standard string level is passed to set_level or at_level, when the level cannot be resolved to an integer, then all logging should be enabled via logging.disable(NOTSET)

task_11.title: Fix --tb=line reporting 'None' when pytrace=False
task_11.description: When running pytest with --tb=line and a test calls pytest.fail(pytrace=False), the terminal output incorrectly displays 'None' instead of the expected failure summary line (e.g., '.../test_foo.py:4: Failed: my message'). The root cause is that the crash-entry lookup did not account for hidden traceback entries produced by pytrace=False, causing a None value to propagate into the terminal reporter. The fix makes the crash-entry resolution aware of hidden traceback entries and ensures downstream rendering components gracefully handle the absence of a crash location.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a test invokes pytest.fail() with pytrace=False and pytest is run in --tb=line mode, the failure line still displays the correct file location and failure message rather than printing the literal text 'None'.

expectation.grounded: ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() must return Optional[ReprFileLocation] instead of always returning ReprFileLocation. When all traceback entries are hidden (as occurs with pytrace=False), it should return None. ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash must accept Optional[ReprFileLocation]. ReprEntry.toterminal() in 'short' style must conditionally render reprfileloc only when it is not None, rather than asserting its presence. In --tb=line mode, when reprcrash is None the reporter must not render the literal string 'None' and should instead produce the correct crash location line or omit the line gracefully.
expectation.conceptual: When a test failure suppresses its traceback via pytrace=False, the crash-entry resolution should recognize that no visible traceback entry exists and signal this absence cleanly. All terminal reporting modes, especially --tb=line, must handle the case where no crash location is available without producing corrupted or misleading output. The failure message and file location should still appear correctly when the information is available.

constraints.grounded: Tests that call pytest.fail() without pytrace=False must continue to produce the same crash location output in all --tb modes (long, short, line, no). The ReprFileLocation returned by _getreprcrash() must still reference the correct file path and line number when visible traceback entries exist. The iteration over traceback entries must respect the ishidden() contract on each entry. Existing serialization and deserialization of ReprExceptionInfo (e.g., for xdist or cacheprovider) must handle reprcrash being None.
constraints.conceptual: Normal traceback reporting for failures that do not suppress pytrace must remain unchanged. The fix must not alter the content or formatting of failure output when traceback entries are visible. Hidden-entry detection must use the existing traceback visibility mechanism and not introduce a separate filtering concept.

behavior: ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() iterates traceback entries from the end, skipping hidden entries, and returns None if all entries are hidden
ReprExceptionInfo.reprcrash is now Optional and can be None when no visible crash entry exists
ReprEntry.toterminal() in 'short' style conditionally renders the file location instead of asserting its presence
In --tb=line mode, when pytrace=False is used, the failure output displays the correct file-location and message line instead of 'None'
When all traceback entries are hidden (pytrace=False), no crash location line is emitted rather than emitting a corrupted 'None' line
acceptance_criteria: When a test calls pytest.fail('my message', pytrace=False) and pytest runs with --tb=line, the FAILURES section displays the file path, line number, and 'Failed: my message' instead of 'None'
When a test calls pytest.fail('my message') without pytrace=False and pytest runs with --tb=line, the output is unchanged from previous behavior
When a test calls pytest.fail('my message', pytrace=False) and pytest runs with --tb=short, no assertion error occurs and the output does not contain 'None'
When a test calls pytest.fail('my message', pytrace=False) and pytest runs with --tb=long or --tb=no, the output remains correct and unaffected
When _getreprcrash() encounters a traceback where all entries are hidden, it returns None rather than raising an exception or returning an invalid object

task_12.title: Fix --last-failed file skipping for non-python test files
task_12.description: The --last-failed (--lf) whole-file skipping optimization (reported as 'skipped N files') did not work for non-python test files. The file-skipping logic only recognized Python Module collectors, so non-python test file collectors (which are File nodes, not Module nodes) were never skipped even when they contained no previously-failed tests. This fix broadens the collector type check from Module to File, adds parent directory paths to the last-failed path set, and correctly resolves Package node paths so that last-failed prioritization and file skipping work uniformly for all test file types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the --last-failed whole-file skipping feature ('skipped N files') works correctly for non-python test files, not only for Python test modules. Previously, when using --last-failed, non-python test files were always collected even if they contained no previously-failed tests, defeating the performance optimization for projects that include non-python tests.

expectation.grounded: The LFPluginCollWrapper and LFPluginCollSkipfiles hooks must check against the File collector base class (from _pytest.nodes) rather than the Module class (from _pytest.python) when deciding whether to skip or filter a collector. Package collectors must still be excluded from file-level skipping since they represent directories, not individual test-bearing files. The LFPlugin.get_last_failed_paths method must return both the paths of previously failed test files and all their parent directory paths, so that directory-level collectors can also be matched. When sorting collectors to prioritize last-failed items, Package nodes must resolve their path to the parent directory (not the __init__.py path) for correct path-set membership checks.
expectation.conceptual: When --last-failed is active, the file-skipping optimization should apply uniformly to all test file types, including non-python test files. Files that contained no previously-failed tests should be skipped regardless of their collector type. The last-failed path prioritization during collection sorting should correctly handle both file-level and package-level collectors.

constraints.grounded: Package collectors must not be treated as skippable test-bearing files; only non-Package File collectors should be candidates for skipping. The existing behavior for Python Module-based test files must not regress, since Module is a subclass of File. The sort stability requirement must be preserved so that last-failed items are prioritized without changing the relative order of other items. The path existence check in get_last_failed_paths must still filter out paths that no longer exist on disk.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not break the existing --last-failed behavior for standard Python test files. Package/directory-level collectors must remain unaffected by file-level skipping. The optimization must correctly handle test files that have been deleted or moved since the last run.

behavior: When --last-failed is used and a non-python test file contains no previously-failed tests, that file's collector is now skipped and counted in the 'skipped N files' report.
The set of last-failed paths now includes parent directories of failed test file paths, enabling correct matching for directory-level and package-level collectors during sort prioritization.
Package collector nodes resolve their comparison path to the parent directory rather than the __init__.py file path when checking membership in the last-failed path set.
File-skipping exclusion logic now correctly identifies Package collectors as non-skippable by checking against the File base class rather than the Module class.
The 'skipped N files' count reported in collection output now accurately reflects all skipped files, including non-python test files.
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest --last-failed on a project with non-python test files where none of those non-python tests previously failed, those non-python test files should be skipped and the 'skipped N files' message should include them in the count.

When running pytest --last-failed on a project with non-python test files where some of those tests did previously fail, only the files containing previously-failed tests should be collected; others should be skipped.
When running pytest --last-failed on a project with standard Python test files, existing file-skipping and prioritization behavior should work identically to before the change.
When running pytest --last-failed, Package collectors should never be skipped by the file-skipping optimization, regardless of whether they are checked against File or Module.

When running pytest --last-failed with previously-failed tests in nested directories, the sort prioritization should correctly place last-failed directories and files first, including correct handling of Package nodes whose path attribute points to __init__.py.

task_13.title: Fix testpaths regression in initial conftest loading
task_13.description: Fixed a regression introduced in pytest 7.3.2 where the testpaths configuration value was always included when discovering initial conftest files, even when explicit test paths were provided on the command line. This caused conftest files from all testpaths directories to be loaded unconditionally, leading to errors such as duplicate addoption conflicts when multiple test suites defined the same CLI options. The fix ensures that testpaths are only considered for initial conftest loading when they are actually in use (i.e., when no explicit paths are given on the command line and the invocation directory matches the root path).

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when explicit test paths are provided on the pytest command line, only conftest files relevant to those explicit paths are loaded during initial conftest discovery. The testpaths configuration value must not cause conftest files from unrelated test directories to be loaded when explicit paths override testpaths. Specifically: (1) Ensure that running 'pytest <explicit_path>' does not load conftest files from other directories listed in testpaths. (2) Ensure that when multiple test suites in testpaths define the same CLI option via parser.addoption, running one suite explicitly does not trigger a duplicate option ValueError from the other suite's conftest. (3) Ensure that testpaths are still used for conftest discovery when no explicit paths are given and the invocation directory matches the root path.

expectation.grounded: When explicit file_or_dir arguments are passed on the command line, Config._decide_args should return those args with ArgsSource.ARGS, and _set_initial_conftests should only iterate over those resolved args for conftest discovery — not concatenate testpaths. When no explicit args are given and the invocation directory equals rootpath, _decide_args should return resolved testpaths with ArgsSource.TESTPATHS. When no explicit args are given and invocation directory differs from rootpath, _decide_args should fall back to the invocation directory with ArgsSource.INCOVATION_DIR. The pytest_load_initial_conftests hook must pre-resolve args via _decide_args before passing them to _set_initial_conftests.
expectation.conceptual: When a user invokes pytest with explicit test paths, only conftest files along the directory hierarchy of those explicit paths should be loaded during startup. The testpaths configuration should only influence conftest discovery when pytest falls back to using testpaths as the source of test collection paths. This prevents cross-contamination of conftest-defined options and hooks between independent test suites.

constraints.grounded: The _set_initial_conftests method must not accept or use testpaths_ini as a parameter. The args passed to _set_initial_conftests must be the fully resolved paths from _decide_args, not the raw namespace.file_or_dir concatenated with testpaths. The _decide_args method must be reusable by both the initial conftest loading phase (pytest_load_initial_conftests) and the full parse phase (parse), ensuring consistent path-resolution logic. When _decide_args is called during early conftest loading, it must not issue warnings (warn=False), reserving warnings for the full parse phase.
constraints.conceptual: The path resolution logic for determining which directories to scan for conftest files must be centralized and consistent between the early conftest loading phase and the full argument parsing phase. Conftest discovery must never load conftest files from directories that are not part of the actual resolved test paths for the current invocation. Existing behavior for testpaths-based discovery when no explicit paths are given must be preserved.

behavior: When explicit paths are provided on the command line, only those paths are used as anchors for initial conftest discovery; testpaths directories are excluded.
When no explicit paths are provided and the invocation directory equals the root path, testpaths are resolved (via glob for non-pyargs mode) and used as conftest discovery anchors.
When no explicit paths are provided and the invocation directory differs from the root path, the invocation directory is used as the sole conftest discovery anchor.
The path-resolution logic (_decide_args) is shared between the early conftest loading hook and the full parse method, ensuring consistent behavior.
During the early conftest loading phase, no warnings are issued even if testpaths resolve to empty; warnings are only issued during the full parse phase.
Conftest files from unrelated testpaths directories are no longer loaded, preventing duplicate addoption ValueError when multiple test suites define the same CLI options.
acceptance_criteria: When a project has multiple directories listed in testpaths (e.g., 'test' and 'unit_test'), each with a conftest.py defining the same addoption option, running 'pytest unit_test' should succeed without a ValueError about duplicate option names.

When running 'pytest <explicit_path>', only conftest files in the directory hierarchy of <explicit_path> should be loaded during initial conftest discovery, not conftest files from other testpaths entries.
When running 'pytest' with no explicit paths from the root directory, conftest files from all testpaths directories should still be loaded as before.
When running 'pytest' with no explicit paths from a non-root directory, conftest discovery should use the current invocation directory, not testpaths.

When testpaths globs resolve to no files and no explicit args are given, no warning should be issued during initial conftest loading, but a PytestConfigWarning should be issued during the full parse phase.

task_14.title: Fix __tracebackhide__ not working with chained exceptions
task_14.description: When using chained exceptions in Python 3 (e.g., catching one exception and raising another), traceback frames marked with __tracebackhide__ = True were still displayed in the output. This happened because the ExceptionInfo context was not correctly threaded through the traceback filtering pipeline for each exception in a chain. The fix restructures how traceback filtering receives exception context: instead of storing a weak reference to ExceptionInfo inside each TracebackEntry, the ExceptionInfo is now passed explicitly at filter-time, ensuring each chained exception is filtered with its own correct context. Additionally, the traceback filtering API was refactored from a mutable in-place pruning model (_prunetraceback mutating excinfo.traceback) to a functional return-value model (_traceback_filter returning a new Traceback), and TracebackEntry was made immutable.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that traceback frames marked with `__tracebackhide__ = True` are properly hidden even when exceptions are chained (via explicit `raise ... from` or implicit context during exception handling). Previously, when a function set `__tracebackhide__ = True` and then re-raised or raised a new exception in a try/except block, the hidden frames were still displayed in the chained exception traceback output. The fix must ensure: (1) hidden frames in the original (cause) exception are suppressed, (2) hidden frames in the new (chained) exception are suppressed, (3) the 'During handling of the above exception...' separator still appears correctly, and (4) when all traceback entries are hidden, a helpful fallback message is shown instead of a crash.

expectation.grounded: TracebackEntry.ishidden() must receive the correct ExceptionInfo for each exception in a chain, so that __tracebackhide__ callables receive the right exception context. Traceback.filter() must accept either an ExceptionInfo instance (to filter hidden entries) or a callable predicate. ExceptionInfo.getrepr() must accept a tbfilter parameter that is either a bool or a Callable[[ExceptionInfo], Traceback]. The Node._traceback_filter() method (replacing _prunetraceback()) must return a Traceback rather than mutating excinfo.traceback in place. When all traceback entries are hidden after filtering, repr_traceback must return a ReprTraceback with a message indicating entries are hidden and suggesting --full-trace. ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() must return Optional[ReprFileLocation], returning None when all entries are hidden.
expectation.conceptual: When a test produces chained exceptions and intermediate helper functions use __tracebackhide__ to suppress their frames, the displayed traceback should only show the user-relevant frames for each exception in the chain. Hidden frames should be consistently suppressed across all parts of the chained traceback output. If all frames in a particular exception's traceback are hidden, the framework should display a clear message directing the user to use --full-trace to see hidden frames, rather than crashing or showing confusing output.

constraints.grounded: TracebackEntry must remain immutable after construction (Final fields); repr_style changes must produce new instances via with_repr_style() rather than mutating in place. Traceback.filter() must not default to filtering without an ExceptionInfo — callers must explicitly pass the ExceptionInfo or a custom filter callable. The _traceback_filter method must not mutate excinfo.traceback; it must return a new Traceback. FormattedExcinfo.tbfilter must support Union[bool, Callable[[ExceptionInfo[BaseException]], Traceback]] without breaking existing bool usage. When tbfilter is False or style is native, no __tracebackhide__ filtering should be applied. Existing behavior for non-chained exceptions and for __tracebackhide__ with callable values must be preserved.
constraints.conceptual: The traceback filtering mechanism must not hold stale or incorrect exception references. Traceback data structures should be treated as immutable to prevent unintended side effects across chained exception processing. Existing traceback display behavior for simple (non-chained) exceptions must not regress. Custom __tracebackhide__ callables that inspect the exception value must still receive the correct exception. The --full-trace flag must continue to bypass all traceback hiding.

behavior: When a function sets __tracebackhide__ = True and the exception is part of a chain (either __cause__ or __context__), the function's frame is now suppressed in the traceback output for that exception in the chain.

Traceback.filter() now requires an explicit argument: either an ExceptionInfo (to filter hidden entries using ishidden) or a callable predicate. It no longer defaults to filtering hidden entries without exception context.
TracebackEntry.ishidden() now takes an explicit ExceptionInfo parameter instead of using an internally stored weak reference, ensuring correct exception context is used for each exception in a chain.
TracebackEntry is now immutable: _rawentry and _repr_style are Final. The set_repr_style() mutator is replaced by with_repr_style() which returns a new TracebackEntry instance.
Node._prunetraceback(excinfo) is renamed to Node._traceback_filter(excinfo) and now returns a Traceback instead of mutating excinfo.traceback in place.
ExceptionInfo.getrepr() tbfilter parameter now accepts Union[bool, Callable[[ExceptionInfo], Traceback]], allowing custom traceback filtering strategies to be passed in.

When all traceback entries are hidden after filtering, the traceback representation includes a message indicating all entries are hidden and suggesting the --full-trace option, instead of potentially raising an error.
ExceptionInfo._getreprcrash() now returns Optional[ReprFileLocation], returning None when all traceback entries are hidden.
When processing chained exceptions, each exception in the chain is now filtered with its own dedicated ExceptionInfo context, preventing cross-contamination of traceback hiding decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Given a test that calls a helper function with __tracebackhide__ = True that catches an exception and raises a different one, when the test fails, the traceback should not show frames from the hidden helper function in either the original or chained exception sections.

Given a test with chained exceptions where all intermediate functions set __tracebackhide__ = True, when viewing the traceback output, only the test function frame and exception information should be visible, with hidden frames suppressed from both the cause and the effect exception tracebacks.
Given a test with chained exceptions and __tracebackhide__ = True on helpers, when running with --full-trace, all frames including hidden ones should be displayed.

Given a test where __tracebackhide__ is set to a callable that inspects the exception, when the exception is part of a chain, the callable should receive the correct ExceptionInfo for that specific exception in the chain.

Given a scenario where all traceback entries for an exception in a chain are hidden, when the traceback is displayed, a message indicating that all entries are hidden with a suggestion to use --full-trace should appear instead of empty output or an error.
Given a test with a simple (non-chained) exception and __tracebackhide__ = True in a helper, when the test fails, the hidden frames should still be suppressed as before (no regression).
When Traceback.filter() is called with an ExceptionInfo argument, it should return a new Traceback containing only entries where ishidden(excinfo) returns False.
When ExceptionInfo.getrepr() is called with a callable tbfilter, the callable should be invoked with the ExceptionInfo and its return value used as the filtered traceback.

task_15.title: Fix UnicodeEncodeError when writing non-ASCII text to debug log file
task_15.description: When pytest is invoked with the --debug flag and test node IDs contain non-ASCII characters (e.g., Cyrillic or accented Latin characters), writing those node IDs to the debug log file raises a UnicodeEncodeError on systems where the default file encoding is not UTF-8 (notably Windows). The fix ensures the debug log file is opened with explicit UTF-8 encoding so all valid Unicode characters in test identifiers can be written successfully. Additionally, related encoding hardening is applied to the towncrier changelog draft script (explicit UTF-8) and the LsofFdLeakChecker subprocess output (explicit locale-preferred encoding).

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running pytest with the --debug option does not raise a UnicodeEncodeError when test node IDs contain non-ASCII characters (e.g., Cyrillic, accented Latin). Previously, on platforms where the default file encoding is not UTF-8, the debug log file could not be written and the test session would crash. Ensure that related file-writing operations across the codebase also use explicit encoding to prevent similar failures.

expectation.grounded: When --debug is supplied, the debug log file opened by pytest_cmdline_parse in the helpconfig module must use UTF-8 encoding. The towncrier draft changelog writer must also open its output file with UTF-8 encoding. The LsofFdLeakChecker subprocess must specify an explicit encoding derived from locale.getpreferredencoding(False) when capturing stdout as text. All three paths must handle the full Unicode range without raising UnicodeEncodeError.
expectation.conceptual: When the user runs pytest with --debug, any test whose node ID contains non-ASCII characters should have its debug information written to the log file without error. The debug log must faithfully represent all Unicode characters present in test identifiers. Ancillary file-writing operations in the tooling should similarly declare their encoding explicitly to avoid platform-dependent encoding failures.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter the content or format of the debug log output beyond encoding. Existing ASCII-only debug logs must remain identical. The LsofFdLeakChecker encoding must reflect the system's preferred encoding (via locale.getpreferredencoding) rather than being hardcoded to UTF-8, since it processes OS-level subprocess output. No new dependencies may be introduced beyond the standard library locale module.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be backward-compatible: debug log files produced for ASCII-only test suites must be unchanged. Platform-specific subprocess interactions must respect the platform's native encoding rather than assuming UTF-8. No existing test behavior or debug output formatting may regress.

behavior: The debug log file is opened with UTF-8 encoding, allowing non-ASCII test node IDs (e.g., containing Cyrillic or accented characters) to be written without raising UnicodeEncodeError.
On platforms with non-UTF-8 default encodings (e.g., Windows with cp1252), the --debug flag no longer causes a crash when encountering non-ASCII characters in test identifiers.
The towncrier changelog draft file is opened with explicit UTF-8 encoding, preventing encoding errors when changelog entries contain non-ASCII text.
The LsofFdLeakChecker subprocess captures stdout using the locale-preferred encoding, ensuring correct decoding of system command output across platforms.
acceptance_criteria: When a test file contains a test function with non-ASCII characters in its name (e.g., def test_чћшђ_čćšđ()) and pytest is invoked with --debug, the test session completes without UnicodeEncodeError and the debug log file contains the non-ASCII node ID.
